description: The three video types Motion Lab produces, and only these. A brief declares one in deliverables.video_type; scripts/studio.py new requires it and validate enforces it. Any type can be a member of a series (specs/series-spec.json), alone or mixed with the others.
margin_note: Each nominal range may be missed by this many seconds at either end. The allowed window is nominal.min - margin to nominal.max + margin; a type with no nominal max has no upper limit.
complexity_note: complexity_budget is what one film of the type can explain (story-writer rulebook 3.1, scope check, added 2026-11-07 from the owner's review of game-theory-trust: 'We can't compress complicated content into a short video.'). A mechanism is a cause-and-effect chain the viewer must follow to reach the payoff. A new term is a concept name, a jargon word, or a named person, study, event, tournament or algorithm the audience must learn; names that appear only in a source line do not count. A named study, event, tournament or algorithm needs its setup (who, what, how it was scored, what happened, why), at least named_case_setup_sec_min seconds. Over budget: cut, split into a series, or move to a longer type. The reel numbers are the owner's ruling; the long-reel and youtube numbers are a first guess, not yet measured.

reel.name: Instagram reel

complexity_budget.named_case_rule: only as the film's whole subject; never a closing beat or a re-hook

reel.note: 45 s is preferred; go toward 60 s only for a complicated topic that needs more animated beats, not more words.

long-reel.name: Long Instagram reel

complexity_budget.alternative: two linked mechanisms and no worked case

long-reel.note: Portrait, up to 3 minutes. Needs a re-hook about every 35-45 s; reel-loop fits only its short end.

youtube.name: YouTube video
youtube.note: Landscape, over 3 minutes, no upper limit. Needs a re-hook every 60-90 s.
